correctness.rationale: Explicit unique path-pair normal forms give total coefficients. Prefix comparison splits surviving squares into equal paths and two strict closed-suffix orientations, proving Q(t). Repeated closed suffixes prove all higher powers remain nonzero. The resolvent and simple Perron pole against a double total-growth pole yield c/n+O(n^-2). The eight-graph product checker corroborates exact coefficients including periodic, acyclic, isolated and primitive cases.

value.rationale: Square-zero behavior is an intrinsic semigroup invariant. The exact all-graph rational count and quantitative Perron c/n transition identify typical high-length nilpotence versus persistent powers, which coarse growth alone does not distinguish. The theorem includes cyclic infinite and acyclic finite semigroups and provides an explicit computable graph constant.
